subject: Science
qualification: International GCSE (9-1) Biology, Chemistry and Physics: three separate subjects (2017 specifications, linear)
specVersion: Biology Issue 3, September 2024; Chemistry Issue 3, September 2024 (its front matter still says Issue 2 in one sentence); Physics Issue 4, September 2024; Science (Double Award) Issue 4, September 2024. First teaching September 2017, first assessment June 2019, first certification August 2019.
statusNote: Re-read on 22 October 2026 as raw text (pdftotext) from the four official Pearson specification PDFs: Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1, Physics 4PH1 and Science (Double Award) 4SD0. Papers, codes, durations, marks, weightings, assessment objectives, command words, practical approach, grading, forbidden combinations, the maths skills table (read from the page image) and every numbered point in all 17 units were compared with the raw text: 176 Biology, 182 Chemistry and 195 Physics points, each paraphrased in this file with its spec number. A trailing B, C or P marks a bold statement: Paper 2 only and not in the Double Award; these match the Double Award PDF's own exclusion lists exactly. Year and term placement is a recommended sequence, not set by the board. The modular 2024 specifications were not read. November 2026 alignment with the school's files: the Year 10 and Year 11 order follows the school's KS4 Biology, Chemistry and Physics intents (Biology 4 ecology before Biology 3 inheritance in Year 11; Physics 8 points 8.1 to 8.10 taught in Year 11). The school's scheme files are generic: Pearson five-year schemes for Edexcel GCSE (9-1) sciences and Oxford's AQA five-year schemes (Kerboodle); each unit's resources name the matching lessons and chapters and list the scheme content that is not on 4SD0 and is not taught.

nonExam: No coursework, no practical endorsement and no separate practical paper. Practical investigations are written into the content as italicised 'practical:' points, and experimental skills (solving problems in practical contexts, planning, variables, measurement, analysis, reliability, evaluation) are examined in the written papers (AO3). Appendix 6 of each specification lists optional extra investigations. Practical points: Biology 2.9, 2.12, 2.14B, 2.17, 2.23, 2.33B, 2.39, 2.45B, 2.50, 2.58B, 3.5, 4.2, 4.4B, 5.6; Chemistry 1.7C, 1.13, 1.36, 1.60C, 2.14, 2.21, 2.42, 2.43C, 3.8, 3.15, 3.16, 4.43C; Physics 1.5, 1.22, 2.9, 2.23P, 3.17, 3.19, 3.25P, 3.27P, 4.9, 5.4, 5.11P, 5.14P, 6.6, 7.6. Double Award keeps the points without a letter: Biology 9, Chemistry 8, Physics 9 practicals. The Double Award papers (4SD0/1B, 1C, 1P) are 110 marks and 33.3% each, 330 marks in total, all taken in the same series. Calculators are allowed but not those that retrieve text or formulae or have QWERTY keyboards. Papers are in English only. Series: November and June. Physics Appendix 7 lists formulae that are not provided in the exam.

gaps: The modular 2024 specifications (4XBI1, 4XCH1, 4XPH1, 4XSD1) and sample assessment materials were not read; this file covers only the linear 2017 specifications.

Double Award statement wording was compared for numbering and exclusions, not word by word against the single-science text; its lists of Biology-only, Chemistry-only and Physics-only points match the B, C and P markings exactly.
Appendix 3 (transferable skills) and Appendix 7 (Periodic Table), the circuit symbols appendix and the glossary were not summarised here.
The Chemistry specification header says Issue 3 (September 2024) but one sentence in it says Issue 2; the header is used.
The qualification web pages give no subject code, so codes come from the specification PDFs (Appendix 1). No 4SD1 linear code exists; 4XSD1 is the modular Double Award.
Year and term placement is a recommended sequence, not set by the board.
The booklet teaches Biology, Chemistry and Physics as three separate International GCSEs, so the Double Award (4SD0) route is withdrawn and every bold (B, C, P) statement is taught.
The booklet's Year 10 and 11 Biology does not list ecology (Section 4) or the use of biological resources (Section 5): both are examined in 4BI1 and stay in Year 11 Spring until the school confirms.
